facts.statement: Acristavus is a genus of saurolophine dinosaur whose name means "non-crested grandfather".
facts.quote: Acristavus (meaning "non-crested grandfather") is a genus of saurolophine dinosaur.

facts.statement: Acristavus lacked skull ornamentation, unlike nearly all other hadrosaurids.
facts.quote: Unlike nearly all hadrosaurids, Acristavus lacked ornamentation on its skull.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen MOR 1155 includes an almost complete skull and associated postcranial bones such as eleven cervical vertebrae and various limb elements.
facts.quote: MOR 1155 consists of an almost complete skull with associated postcrania including eleven cervical vertebrae, three incomplete dorsal vertebrae, a proximal caudal vertebra, several dorsal ribs, the left humerus, the left ulna, the right sternal, the left pubis, the left femur, the left tibia, two left metatarsals, five left pedal phalanges and one right pedal phalanx.

facts.statement: Acristavus is significant because it suggests that the ancestor of all hadrosaurids lacked cranial ornamentation, which evolved independently in later subfamilies.
facts.quote: The discovery of Acristavus is paleontologically significant because it supports the position that the ancestor of all hadrosaurids did not possess cranial ornamentation, and that ornamentation was an adaptation that later arose interdependently in the subfamilies Saurolophinae and Lambeosaurinae.

facts.statement: The type species A. gagslarsoni was named in 2011.
facts.quote: The type species A. gagslarsoni was named in 2011.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen MOR 1155 was recovered from the Two Medicine Formation in Teton County, Montana.
facts.quote: The holotype specimen of Acristavus, MOR 1155, was recovered at the Two Medicine Formation, in Teton County, Montana.

facts.statement: A second specimen, UMNHVP 16607, was assigned to Acristavus in 2011 after being excavated from the Wahweap Formation in Utah.
facts.quote: A second specimen UMNHVP 16607 assigned to Acristavus in 2011, was excavated from the Smokey Mountain Road locality in the Reynolds Point Member of the Wahweap Formation in Utah.

facts.statement: The holotype was collected from rock deposited during the Campanian stage of the Cretaceous, approximately 79 million years ago.
facts.quote: The specimen was collected in 1999 by C. Riley Nelson in well-indurated tan colored calcareous sandstone that was deposited during the Campanian stage of the Cretaceous period, approximately 79 million years ago.

facts.statement: Acristavus lived during a time when the Western Interior Seaway was at its widest, isolating southern Laramidia from the rest of North America.
facts.quote: During the time that Acristavus lived, the Western Interior Seaway was at its widest extent, almost completely isolating southern Laramidia off from the rest of North America.

facts.statement: Acristavus inhabited an environment containing lakes, floodplains, and east-flowing rivers.
facts.quote: The area where dinosaurs lived included lakes, floodplains, and east-flowing rivers.

facts.statement: Acristavus was assigned to the basal position within the Brachylophosaurini by Gates et al. in 2011.
facts.quote: Acristavus was first assigned to the Brachylophosaurini, in a basal position, by Gates et al. (2011).

facts.statement: Brachylophosaurines, the tribe containing Acristavus, are derived members of the group Saurolophinae.
facts.quote: Brachylophosaurines are derived members of the group Saurolophinae.

facts.statement: Acristavus is classified within the family Hadrosauridae.
facts.quote: familia: Hadrosauridae

facts.statement: Acristavus belongs to the tribe Brachylophosaurini.
facts.quote: tribus: Brachylophosaurini

facts.statement: Acristavus was a medium-sized duck-billed dinosaur reaching 8.5 meters in length, 2.5 meters in height, and weighing an estimated 2.5 tonnes.
facts.quote: Acristavus era un dinosaurio pico de pato de tamaño medio, llegando a medir 8,5 metros de largo, 2,5 de alto y con un peso estimado en 2,5 toneladas.

facts.statement: Acristavus shared its environment with dinosaurs including the lambeosaur Adelolophus, the ceratopsian Diabloceratops, ankylosaurs, pachycephalosaurs, and the theropod Lythronax, which was likely the apex predator.
facts.quote: Acristavus shared its paleoenvironment with other dinosaurs, such as the lambeosaur Adelolophus hutchisoni, the ceratopsian Diabloceratops eatoni, unnamed ankylosaurs and pachycephalosaurs, and the theropod Lythronax argestes, which was likely the apex predator in its ecosystem.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Acristavus and Maiasaura are sister taxa, as recent analysis suggests Maiasaura is more closely related to Brachylophosaurus.
facts.quote: Gates concluded that Acristavus and Maiasaura shared a sister-taxon relationship but more recent analysis by Prieto-Márquez (2013) shows that Maiasaura is more closely related to the more derived Brachylophosaurus.

facts.statement: Researchers initially assigned Acristavus to the basal position within the Brachylophosaurini tribe.
facts.quote: Acristavus fue asignado inicialmente a la tribu Brachylophosaurini, en una posición basal, por Gates et al.

facts.statement: Subsequent phylogenetic analyses have confirmed that Acristavus belongs to the Brachylophosaurini tribe.
facts.quote: Todos los análisis filogenéticos posteriores han confirmado esta asignación.

facts.statement: The Brachylophosaurini tribe consists of derived members of the Saurolophinae subfamily.
facts.quote: Brachylophosaurini es una tribu de miembros derivados de la subfamilia Saurolophinae

facts.statement: Gates concluded that Acristavus and Maiasaura share a sister-taxon relationship.
facts.quote: Gates concluye que Acristavus y Maiasaura comparten una relación de taxón hermano

facts.statement: A more recent analysis by Prieto-Márquez suggests Maiasaura is more closely related to the advanced Brachylophosaurus than to Acristavus.
facts.quote: un análisis más reciente de Prieto-Márquez muestra que Maiasaura esta más cercanamente relacionado con el más avanzado Brachylophosaurus

facts.statement: The parent group of Acristavus is the Brachylophosaurini.
facts.quote: Parent group: Brachylophosaurini

facts.statement: Acristavus belongs to the class Ornithischia.
facts.quote: Class: Ornithischia

facts.statement: Acristavus lived during the Campanian stage, between 83.6 and 72.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Campanian (83.6 to 72.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: The Wahweap Formation, where Acristavus fossils were found, has been radiometrically dated between 81 and 76 million years ago.
facts.quote: La formación Wahweap ha sido datada radiométricamente entre 81 y 76 millones de años atrás.

facts.statement: The Wahweap Formation is part of the Grand Staircase region, extending south of Bryce Canyon National Park through Zion National Park and into the Grand Canyon.
facts.quote: La formación Wahweap es parte de la región Grand Staircase, una inmensa sucesión de capas de rocas sedimentarias que se extienden al sur del Parque Nacional Bryce Canyon a través del Parque Nacional Zion y en el Gran Cañón.

facts.statement: The habitat of Acristavus included lakes, rivers, and floodplains that flowed eastward.
facts.quote: La zona en la que vivían los dinosaurios incluye lagos, ríos y llanuras de inundación, que fluían hacia el este.

facts.statement: Evidence of rapid sedimentation suggests Acristavus lived in a humid, seasonal climate.
facts.quote: La presencia de una rápida sedimentación y otras evidencias sugieren un clima húmedo, de temporada.

facts.statement: In the Wahweap Formation, Acristavus coexisted with the ceratopsian Diabloceratops, the lambeosaurine Adelolophus, the ceratopsian Diabloceratops eatoni, and the tyrannosaurid Lythronax argestes.
facts.quote: Por la parte de Wahwaeap, coexistió con el ceratopsiano Diabloceratops, con el lambeosaurino Adelolophus el ceratopsiano Diabloceratops eatoni, y el tiranosáurido Lythronax argestes

facts.statement: Other vertebrates living alongside Acristavus in the Wahweap Formation included freshwater fish, rays, sharks, turtles like Compsemys, crocodilians, and lungfish.
facts.quote: Otros vertebrados en la Formación Wahweap que convivieron con Acristavus incluyen peces de agua dulce, amias, abundantes rayass y tiburones, tortugas como Compsemys, crocodilianos, y peces pulmonados.

facts.statement: A unique fossil trackway discovered in 2010 suggests a predator-prey relationship between dinosaurs and primitive mammals in the region.
facts.quote: En 2010 se descubrió un rastro fósil único que sugiere una relación depredador-presa entre los dinosaurios y los mamíferos primitivos.

facts.statement: The fossil trackway includes at least two fossilized mammal burrows and excavation slots presumably caused by a maniraptoran dinosaur.
facts.quote: El rastro fósil incluye al menos dos madrigueras fosilizadas de mamíferos, así como ranuras de excavación asociadas presumiblemente causadas por un dinosaurio maniraptor.

facts.statement: In the Dos Medicinas Formation, Acristavus shared its niche in the lower part of the formation with Gryposaurus latidens and some dromaeosaurids.
facts.quote: Por otro lado, en la mejor documentada Formación Dos Medicinas, compartió nicho en la parte baja de dicha formación con Gryposaurus latidens y algunos dromeosáuridos.

facts.statement: There are currently two recorded fossil occurrences of Acristavus.
facts.quote: Fossil occurrences recorded: 2
